newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe 1997 wheat exports seen at 35,000 T.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe 1997 wheat exports seen at 35,000 T.

text.p: Farmers in Zimbabwe are set to export 35,000 tonnes of wheat this season, 65 percent short of the export quota sanctioned by the government last November, an official said on Wednesday.

Commercial Cereal Producers Association Chairman Peter Wells told reporters although the government had doubled to 100,000 tonnes the amount of the cereal crop farmers could export directly, producers had shown little interest in the export market because of a fall in international prices.
"There is very little interest on the export market. When we asked for export permits about six months ago the world prices were good. Now they have fallen," Wells said.
He said wheat prices had fallen to Z$2,400 per tonne from around Z$3,000 a tonne last year, largely due to bumper harvests in Australia and Argentina.

The Zimbabwe government opened up wheat exports -- previously restricted to the state-owned Grain Marketing Board-- last July following an outcry from farmers that this was hampering production of the cereal in the July 1997 to June 1998 season.
